text:
Ana (Finance): Anyone else noticing a new 'GPU-SUPPORT-SURCHARGE' line on the March invoice for europe-west3? ~18k. Not present in previous months. :thinking_face:
Sam L (Infra): Can you paste the exact line(s)? a CSV snippet or screenshot would help.
Ana (Finance): Sure — copied from the billing export for project redwood-infra:
```
resource_id,sku_description,sku_id,cost_usd,project_id,usage_start_time
projects/12345/zones/europe-west3-a/instances/gpu-eu-3-7a,NVIDIA A100 (onDemand),SKU:GPU-A100-OD,45000.00,redwood-infra,2026-03-10T12:01:00Z
projects/12345/zones/europe-west3-a/instances/gpu-eu-3-7a,GPU-SUPPORT-SURCHARGE - NVIDIA A100,SKU:GPU-SUPP-001,18000.00,redwood-infra,2026-03-10T12:01:00Z
projects/12345,Committed Use Discount - GPUs,SKU:CUD-GPU-2025,-20000.00,redwood-infra,2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
```
Kai R (SRE): :eyes: That looks like a separate marketplace/vendor meter rather than a duplicate compute charge. If we installed a marketplace image or driver that meters per GPU it could show as an extra SKU.
Meera C (CloudOps): We rolled the new nvidia driver packaging last month in the eu-west3 node-pool (k8s nodegroup 'gpu-eu-west3-prod'). The image uses the marketplace package 'nvidia-driver-pro' via a startup-script — I flagged it in the deploy PR.
Sam L (Infra): Marketplace meters won't be covered by the CUDs for compute. That would explain the extra amount instead of a duplicate compute line. Still, need to confirm if the meter is expected and whether it was applied multiple times during boot.
Kai R (SRE): Run this quick BigQuery to group by SKU in March and confirm totals:
```sql
SELECT sku.description AS sku, SUM(cost) AS total_cost
FROM `billing.gcp_export.redwood_billing.*`
WHERE project.id = 'redwood-infra'
  AND DATE(_PARTITIONTIME) BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-31'
  AND sku.description LIKE '%GPU%'
GROUP BY sku
ORDER BY total_cost DESC;
```
Ana (Finance): Ran it — results (trimmed):
```
NVIDIA A100 (onDemand)            45000.00
GPU-SUPPORT-SURCHARGE - NVIDIA A100 18000.00
Committed Use Discount - GPUs      -20000.00
```
Ana (Finance): Net GPU-related cost still higher than expected because the marketplace surcharge is additive.
Meera C (CloudOps): I also checked kube logs for the node bootstrap (gpu-eu-3-7a) — startup-script shows it installed 'nvidia-driver-pro' and then executed a post-install license activation call to a vendor endpoint. That activation likely triggered a meter event.
Sam L (Infra): Meera, can you pull the node startup logs + the marketplace subscription / order ID from the deployment manifest? We need the vendor meter ID to open a billing case.
Meera C (CloudOps): On it. Also adding that cluster autoscaler did multiple ephemeral scale-ups during March 10-12 due to a job storm; each new node would re-run the startup-script and might have generated multiple license meter events.
Kai R (SRE): Good catch — that would multiply the surcharge. We should repro by creating one test node with the same startup script and watch the billing export for the SKU event. I'll set that up in a small test project.
Sam L (Infra): I'll open a case with cloud billing + the marketplace vendor. Finance, please track this as F-3421. Meera, when you have the subscription/order id please post it here and cc finance@redwood.com.
billing-bot: Ticket created: CB-987654 (cloud billing). Linked to finance F-3421. Priority: P2. :white_check_mark:
Ana (Finance): Thanks — if the vendor confirms this is a metered marketplace fee we'll need to decide: 1) repackage driver into our base image to avoid marketplace metering or 2) bite the surcharge and negotiate bulk pricing. We'll evaluate after vendor response.
Kai R (SRE): I'll test repro and report back by EOD. :thumbsup:
